author: Sun staff
title: Ocean Community YMCA celebrates largest Race4Chase team yet at Newport triathlon | Daily-news-alerts | thewesterlysun.com
text:
WESTERLY — Thirty-five young athletes from the Ocean Community YMCA celebrated a summer of hard work, determination, and growth as they completed the Race4Chase Youth Triathlon in Newport on Aug 9. This year marked the Y’s largest Race4Chase group to date.
With generous support from lead sponsor Washington Trust Company, participants spent eight weeks training in swimming, biking, and running while building confidence, perseverance, and teamwork. For six participants, that journey included an especially exciting milestone: beginning the program riding bikes with training wheels and learning to ride independently in time to complete the triathlon on two wheels.
Race4Chase was created by the Chase Michael Anthony Kowalski (CMAK) Sandy Hook Memorial Foundation in memory of Chase Kowalski, who lost his life in the Sandy Hook Elementary School tragedy in 2012. Chase loved athletics and, at just six years old, completed his first triathlon and won his age group. Race4Chase carries his spirit forward by giving children the opportunity to discover the sport he loved while building healthy habits, confidence, and a belief in what they can accomplish.
“Watching these kids grow throughout the summer is what makes Race4Chase so special,” said Brian Buckley, sports director at the YMCA. “Crossing the finish line is exciting, but we are just as proud of everything it took to get there. They tried new things, overcame challenges, supported one another, and discovered what they are capable of.”
This year’s program was also strengthened by a robust network of local community partners.
Mystic Cycle Centre donated bicycles and helmets, helping ensure participants had the equipment they needed to train and compete. Representatives from Kelly’s Pace in Olde Mistick Village spent time with participants discussing proper footwear selection and safe, successful training, while the WARM Center in Westerly provided snacks and lunches for participants throughout the eight-week program, helping keep the young athletes fueled along the way. Westerly Community Credit Union also provided additional financial support for the program.
These partnerships, together with the leadership of Washington Trust Company, helped create a summer experience that extended well beyond preparing for a single race. Whether learning to ride a bike independently, becoming more comfortable in the water, running farther than they thought they could, or gaining the confidence to try something new, each participant had something worth celebrating.
"The Ocean Community YMCA is incredibly proud of all 35 Race4Chase participants and grateful to Washington Trust Company, Westerly Community Credit Union, Mystic Cycle Centre, Kelly’s Pace, the WARM Center, and the coaches, families and volunteers who helped make this year’s program possible," the YMCA said in a news release.
